## Trump Defends Tariff Policy

Despite facing significant electoral setbacks in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump has doubled down on his tariff strategy, warning foreign companies that failure to build factories in the United States could result in tariffs reaching as high as 300.00%. Trump made these remarks during a meeting with journalists at the White House, emphasizing that removing tariffs would lead to a halt in domestic factory construction and a resumption of imports from China, Japan, and South Korea. The president indicated that substantial policy announcements would come within the next one to two weeks, signaling the continuation of his aggressive trade stance regardless of recent political losses.

## Korean Stocks Plunge Amid Global AI Concerns

The Korean stock market experienced a devastating day on November sixth, with the KOSPI plunging 8.00% and breaking through the critical 5,000 mark for the first time in approximately nine months. Both the circuit breaker and selling side car mechanisms were triggered during the trading session, reflecting the severity of the sell-off. The KOSDAQ index fell 7.00%, with leading semiconductor companies Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each declining 10.00%. This represents the worst single day for Korean equities comparable to the financial crisis of 2008, driven by concerns over artificial intelligence overinvestment and shifting regulatory expectations following the Democratic Party's strong performance in United States midterm elections.

## Semiconductor Demand Uncertainty

The anticipated slowdown in artificial intelligence data center construction in the United States has cast doubt on Korean semiconductor manufacturers' expansion plans. Concerns have emerged that delays in American data center development could negatively impact orders for high-bandwidth memory, dynamic random-access memory, and other semiconductor products. The Honam semiconductor cluster development project, which represents a significant investment commitment by domestic chipmakers, may face headwinds as regulatory uncertainty increases. Industry analysts warn that reduced global semiconductor demand could substantially impact the trajectory of these ambitious capital expenditure programs.

## Deputy Prime Minister Lee Reassures Markets

Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lee Hyung-il convened an emergency external economic ministers meeting to address market volatility and reassure investors. Lee acknowledged that the sharp decline in United States stock markets could trigger global economic spillovers and emphasized the government's commitment to preventing overreaction. He noted that the government will continue implementing core economic policies regardless of changes in American political circumstances, and reaffirmed expectations that annual exports will reach one trillion dollars. The administration pledged to actively monitor United States tariff policies and export controls while maintaining close coordination with international partners.

## American Labor Market Shows Unexpected Strength

Contrary to some economic forecasts, the United States added robust employment in October, with unemployment declining to 4.10%, down 1.00% from previous levels. Wage growth exceeded market expectations, strengthening the case for the Federal Reserve to consider additional rate increases at the December Federal Open Market Committee meeting. This contradictory economic signal—strong labor markets coupled with artificial intelligence investment concerns—has created uncertainty about the Federal Reserve's future policy direction and complicated the outlook for global interest rates.

## European Fiscal Pressures Mount

France's government faced significant setbacks as voters rejected austerity budget measures, with approximately 600,000 citizens participating in protests against proposed spending cuts. France faces a fiscal deficit equivalent to roughly 5.00% of gross domestic product, and forecasts indicate the national debt will rise to 121.70% of GDP by next year if current trends continue. The budget rejection underscores growing public resistance to austerity measures across Europe and raises questions about the sustainability of government finances. Similar fiscal challenges plague multiple European economies, complicating the region's economic recovery prospects.

## United States Treasury Market Rallies

As equity markets deteriorated sharply, investors sought safety in government bonds, causing the ten-year United States Treasury yield to decline 5.70 basis points to 4.84%, marking the lowest level in two months. This flight to quality reflects heightened risk aversion and expectations that economic concerns may prompt the Federal Reserve to moderate its interest rate tightening trajectory. The rally in fixed income assets suggests market participants are pricing in slower economic growth and potentially lower inflation ahead.

## Taiwan and China Markets Suffer Severe Declines

Taiwan's equity market plunged over 9.00%, recording the single largest intraday decline in its history, as semiconductor stocks led the sell-off. Chinese investors withdrew approximately 610 trillion won during the fourth quarter, according to market reports. China's ten-year government bond yield reached 1.58%, marking an all-time low, as capital fled to the safest available assets amid concerns about technology sector regulation and semiconductor demand destruction.

## Regional Cooperation in AI and Physical AI

Despite global market turbulence, Korea and Japan are advancing bilateral economic cooperation in artificial intelligence and semiconductor sectors. The Korea International Trade Association held the sixth Korea-Japan Economic Round Table discussion, focusing on deepening economic cooperation in the artificial intelligence era and strengthening economic security coordination. The meeting emphasized leveraging Korea's semiconductor manufacturing expertise alongside Japan's robotics capabilities to develop physical artificial intelligence solutions, positioning both nations competitively in emerging technology markets.

## Data Center Uncertainty Threatens Battery and EV Investments

Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced plans to build data centers in space, a reaction to Democratic Party regulatory proposals targeting terrestrial data center construction. Texas's newly elected Democratic state senator pledged to halt data center construction projects, citing environmental and power grid concerns. These policy shifts threaten Korean battery manufacturers and electric vehicle producers that had anticipated growth from expanded data center infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence deployment.

## Government Mobilizes Growth Funds

The National Growth Fund is providing 1.7 trillion won in financial support for Hyundai Motor Group's artificial intelligence data center project at Saemangeum, with the Special Purpose Company potentially holding up to 49.00% equity stake. This initiative represents the government's commitment to supporting the three mega-projects of semiconductors, physical artificial intelligence, and artificial intelligence data centers through policy financing mechanisms. The Hyundai project will secure high-performance graphics processing units essential for advanced artificial intelligence computing.

## For Investors and Viewers

The market turbulence reflects fundamental uncertainty about artificial intelligence investment sustainability and regulatory environments globally. Investors should prepare for continued volatility as policy clarity emerges regarding data center construction regulations and trade policies. The Bank of Korea and United States Federal Reserve policy decisions in coming weeks will prove critical for determining market direction. Korean exporters face headwinds from both potential tariff escalation and weakening semiconductor demand, while domestic-focused companies may benefit from government support measures. Diversification across asset classes and careful attention to policy announcements remain essential during this uncertain period.
headline: Global Markets in Turmoil as AI Concerns Trigger Korean Stock Panic
